text:
mike: Quick follow-up on routing scoring — proposal idea:
mike: introduce a short-term 'cost_window' signal (sliding window of recent per-tenant token spend) that amplifies cost weight when sustained high throughput hits a tenant. intent: prefer cheaper model variants for sustained bursts while keeping single-request latency SLOs intact.
anya: curious — how do you keep tail latency safe? if cost_window pushes cheap variant that spikes latency, customers will notice.
ravi: agree with Anya. we should clamp the cost influence so latency SLO is an invariant. something like:
ravi: ```
score = w_latency * norm_latency + w_cost * norm_cost * cost_boost + w_tier * tier_penalty
cost_boost = min(1, recent_cost / cost_window_threshold)
``` 
ravi: where norm_* are 0..1 normalized metrics and latency SLO acts as a hard cutoff before route change.
liz: also add a per-tenant "grace" budget so a cold burst doesn't instantly flip routing. we have to avoid oscillation across models.
anya: +1 on grace. also we need eviction semantics for the sliding window when tenants go quiet, otherwise legacy bursts will keep biasing forever.
mike: implementation notes I had in mind:
mike: - maintain per-tenant rolling counters in the route-resolver cache (cost_tokens, last_update)
mike: - compute cost_boost on resolver evaluation; expose TTL so policies can tune how quickly it decays
mike: - add a runtime flag to enforce latency hard cutoff: if predicted_p99(model) > tenant_p99_slo => treat as disallowed
mike: - fallback ordering: prefer same-region cheaper variant, then cross-region cheap, then expensive same-region
policy-bot: RFC link: https://redwood.rfd/smart-routing-cost-window (draft)
ravi: small concern: how expensive is per-tenant rolling state at scale? we have ~10k tenants on hosted, naive per-tenant objects are heavy.
liz: use compact sketches + approximate expire. we can bucket tenants by recent spend tier and keep exact counters only for top N.
anya: we should add a simulation harness before rollout. create a synthetic workload with spike patterns and measure 
anya: - model-change frequency
anya: - p95/p99 regressions
anya: - churn in route assignments
mike: agreed. plan: I'll add a sim in eng-runtime repo, default policy params: cost_window=5m, grace_tokens=200k, decay_half_life=2m, latency_cutoff_factor=1.2
ravi: please also include an A/B evaluation plan: 10% traffic can go through the new resolver, fallback to current resolver on any error.
liz: ops note: make sure console dashboards surface the cost_window metric per tenant and an alert when model flip rate > threshold.
mike: cool. I'll spin up the RFC follow-up doc with config examples and a sim checklist.
mike: thanks all :thumbsup:
